trap_point: FIFO = Queue. LIFO = FILO = Stack. option  (b) LIFO and (c) FILO are both correct for Stack. Book chose FILO.
memory_trick: STACK = plates stacked. Last plate added is First removed = LIFO = FILO.
one_line_fact: Stack = LIFO = FILO. Last item pushed is First item popped.

question_hindi: एक टेबल जो डाटा रिडेन्डेन्सी जैसी विसंगतियाँ प्रदर्शित करती है-
question_english: A table that exhibits anomalies like data redundancy is subject to?
explanation: Data redundancy leads to three types of anomalies: Update Anomaly (changing data in one place doesn't update all), Insertion Anomaly (can't add data without other data), Deletion Anomaly (deleting data removes other needed data).
trap_point: Redundancy causes ALL THREE anomalies: Update, Insertion, AND Deletion anomalies. Not just one.
memory_trick: Redundancy → UIDs: Update anomaly, Insertion anomaly, Deletion anomaly. All three.
one_line_fact: Data redundancy causes Update, Insertion, AND Deletion anomalies — all three.

question_hindi: एक क्वेरी का प्रकार जो किसी अन्य Query के WHERE या HAVING clause में रखी जाती है, कहलाता है?
question_english: A type of query placed inside the WHERE or HAVING clause of another query is called?
explanation: Sub-query (nested query) is placed within the WHERE or HAVING clause of another (outer) query. Same as Q71.
trap_point: Repeat question of BCI-DBMS-071. Sub-query = nested query inside WHERE/HAVING.
memory_trick: SUB = nested inside another. Sub-query = inside WHERE/HAVING clause.
one_line_fact: Sub-query = query placed inside WHERE or HAVING clause of another query.

question_hindi: एक ट्रांजिशन पूर्ण होने पर इसका execution कहलाता है?
question_english: When a transaction completes successfully, its execution is called?
explanation: A successfully completed transaction is COMMITTED. An unsuccessful transaction is ABORTED/ROLLED BACK. Failed = aborted transaction.
trap_point: Committed = success. Rolled back = failure/undo. Aborted = terminated without commit.
memory_trick: COMMIT = complete success. ROLLBACK = undo failure. Committed = successfully finished.
one_line_fact: Committed = transaction completed successfully with permanent changes.

question_hindi: DCL ......... की तरह कार्य करने की कमाण्ड उपलब्ध कराता है?
question_english: DCL provides commands to work like?
options: (b) Insert, Update or Delete Records And Data Values
(c) Authorizing Access and Other Control Over Database
correct_answer: (c) Authorizing Access and Other Control Over Database
explanation: DCL = Data Control Language. It controls access to database. Commands: GRANT (give privileges) and REVOKE (remove privileges). DCL is for authorization and access control.
trap_point: (a) = DDL (structure). (b) = DML (data manipulation). (c) = DCL (access control). Each language has specific purpose.
memory_trick: DCL = Data CONTROL Language. Controls = access, permissions, security. GRANT & REVOKE are DCL.
one_line_fact: DCL = Data Control Language. Commands: GRANT, REVOKE. Controls database access.

question_hindi: एक डेटाबेस में आपको डाटा को एक्सेस या मैन्टेन करने की अनुमति प्रदान करने वाली Language है?
question_english: Which language in a database provides permission to access or maintain data?
explanation: DCL (Data Control Language) provides commands (GRANT, REVOKE) to control access permissions for database users.
trap_point: DML = manipulates data. DDL = defines structure. DCL = controls ACCESS (permissions).
memory_trick: DCL = Data Control Language = who can ACCESS what.
one_line_fact: DCL = provides access/permission control for database (GRANT and REVOKE).

question_hindi: निम्न में से कौनसा की-वर्ड Data Control Language (DCL) में प्रयुक्त होता है?
question_english: Which keyword is used in Data Control Language (DCL)?
explanation: GRANT is a DCL command that gives privileges to users. SELECT, INSERT, DELETE are DML commands. GRANT and REVOKE are the two main DCL commands.
trap_point: SELECT/INSERT/DELETE = DML. GRANT/REVOKE = DCL. Students confuse DML and DCL commands.
memory_trick: DCL = GRANT + REVOKE. Everything else (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) = DML.
one_line_fact: DCL keywords: GRANT (give permissions) and REVOKE (remove permissions).

question_hindi: ..... Clause एक एडिशनल फिल्टर है जो किसी Result पर apply किया जाता है?
question_english: _____ Clause is an additional filter applied on a Result?
explanation: HAVING clause is an additional filter applied to GROUP BY results. WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after grouping. Same as Q38.
trap_point: Repeat of Q38. HAVING = filter AFTER GROUP BY. WHERE = filter BEFORE grouping.
memory_trick: HAVING = extra filter on grouped results. Comes after GROUP BY.
one_line_fact: HAVING = additional filter on GROUP BY results (applied after grouping).
